narr: Moisture continued to flow northward across northern Arizona as the weakening remnants of Kay were post-tropical and located southwest of San Diego. The low level moisture |brought showers and thunderstorms to the area.
ev: The river gauge at the Village of Supai showed a 1.83 foot rise at 1045 AM. The stream gauge at the confluence with the Colorado River (about 10 miles down stream from the Village of Supai) had a 5.5 foot rise in about 45 minutes at 1145 AM. The crest was at 12.57 feet with a flow of 1735 CFS. Base flow is at about 7 feet with a flow of 70 CFS.
A river gauge on the Paria River near the Colorado River showed a 1.83 foot rise at 545 PM MST.
Heavy rain over the Tunnel and Pipeline fire scar caused flash flooding across Highway 89. The highway closed in both directions at mile marker 430 from 108 PM until 440 PM.
Flash flooding was reported about 10 miles north of Joseph City at the intersection of Blairs Spring Wash and North Porter Road. The dirt road was washed out by the flooding and a vehicle got stuck.
